what: A lane with a 200K context that must not read whole files spent over half of it reading the functions a part read crosses (Reads, the walk, the engine, the carry, the session's post, seed and queue), because a read of a step's value is special-cased by `ReadKind::STEP` in six places across four files with no one function that says what a kernel-answered read is. The exhaustive model in exhaustive/nested.rs (619 lines) could then not be read and extended in the same lane, so the three controls of part reads were written as a smaller exhaustive check in tests/cost.rs and the model's way is owed.
cost: the brief's exhaustive piece moved to a successor lane; piece 2 (maintained steps) not started
whys: why half the context went to reading: a step read is valued in `Walk::now`, `Engine::now`, `Reads::step`, `Session::post`, `Session::seed` and `Kernel::describe`, each by its own `kind == STEP` test
why six places: the first step read was added as a special case of a world read, and nothing since gathered the cases
why the model was out of reach: nest.rs and session.rs are over 1,100 lines each, and the model can only be extended by someone who has read both it and them
cause: the kinds of read the kernel answers itself had no single home: each consumer tested for the one kind there was
class: a second case of something special-cased by an equality test in many places costs a reading of every place
prevention: `table::split(read)` is now the one function that says which step, and what of its value, a kernel-answered read is of, and `ReadKind::is_kernels` the one test; a new kernel kind is added there
fix: done for the lookup, the run, the session and the carry; owed: the table step as a way of the model in exhaustive/nested.rs
